body_markdown:
Hey all,


Back in 2024, Opera was the[first major browser](https://press.opera.com/2024/04/03/ai-feature-drops-local-llms/) to give built-in access to local AI models in an experimental developer build. Since then, advances in open-weight models and consumer hardware have made running AI on your computer more practical.


At the same time, developers want to build AI into their sites and extensions without sending every request to the cloud, paying for every token, or tying their users to one vendor’s model. Many would rather hand that work to AI running on the user’s own computer.


Today, we’re starting a bigger push into local AI, making it a central part of our browsers. The first step is WebAI, now in early preview across Opera One, Opera GX and Opera Neon. With local AI built into the browser, you can start creating your own browser capabilities instead of waiting for software companies to build them.


“A lot of what people want from AI doesn’t need a data center. Your laptop can already do it, without sending your data anywhere,” said Krystian Kolondra, EVP Browsers and AI, Opera. “We first shipped local models to developers in 2024. Now we’re bringing them to everyone. More models and tools are coming, and you’ll always decide what runs on your machine.”


Introducing WebAI, a new way for websites and browser extensions to use AI models running locally on your device. Watch the video to see how it works.


# What is WebAI?


WebAI lets websites and extensions use AI that runs locally, in your browser. People want AI to do more than answer questions in a chat window. They want it to work with the pages they’re on, and WebAI makes that possible.


WebAI is a proposed web standard, backed by companies including Google and Microsoft. Opera’s implementation lets developers use a range of AI models directly in the browser, including open-weight models running on Opera’s inference engine.


Local inference is built into the browser, so there’s no separate AI app to install, no local server to configure and no API key to get. Because the AI runs on your computer, the content it processes doesn’t need to be sent to a cloud AI provider.


WebAI works with different compatible local models, including open-weight models provided through Opera and compatible models already on your device, so you’re not tied to a single model provider.


## You’re always in control


WebAI is opt-in. Nothing is downloaded until you turn it on in Settings, and you can turn it off at any time.


# Why it matters for developers


WebAI introduces the Prompt, Decision and Semantic Embeddings APIs. With them, developers can generate text, classify information and find relationships between pieces of content: building blocks for tools that do more than answer questions.


For developers, especially independent developers and small teams, WebAI means:


- **Peace of mind for your users:** page data can stay on their device when the AI uses it
- **No per-request cloud costs,** and no AI infrastructure to run


It also makes it easy for anyone using AI coding tools to build their own personal extensions. For example, one that spots relevant job postings, prioritizes the articles you should read, highlights information that matches your interests, or makes your saved content searchable, all without running an external AI service.


# See what it can do


To show what developers could build, our team made six experimental extensions. They’re examples to spark ideas, not Opera features:


- [Project Lens](https://addons.opera.com/extensions/details/project-lens/) : Tell it what you’re working on, and it colors any article by how much each paragraph matters to your project
- [Got It?](https://addons.opera.com/extensions/details/got-it/) : Writes a quick quiz about the article you just read, so you can check you understood it
- [Questionable Intelligence](https://addons.opera.com/extensions/details/questionable-intelligence/) : Asks playful questions about the article you’re on and draws the verdict as a chart
- [Semantic Art](https://addons.opera.com/extensions/details/semantic-art/) : Turns an article into moving art, with similar sentences becoming visual neighbors
- [RecordIn Alchemy](https://addons.opera.com/extensions/details/recordin-alchemy/) : Turns any article into an insufferably inspirational social media post
- [C·I·A·O (Cat Intelligence at Opera)](https://addons.opera.com/extensions/details/ciao-cat-intelligence-at-opera/) : Two ASCII cats improvise a scene on any topic you give them


You’ll find the full list of supported APIs and developer documentation at[next.opera.com/web-ai](https://next.opera.com/web-ai/) .


## How do I try it?


1. Download or update[Opera One](https://www.opera.com/one)
2. Go to **Settings** → **Opera AI** and turn on **Enable Web AI API** . This downloads a compatible local model, so it may take a few minutes
3. Install one of the example extensions above and open it from your extensions menu


WebAI is an early preview, available on Windows PC (64-bit, Intel/AMD) and Macs with Apple silicon. It isn’t available on Intel-based Macs, Linux or Windows on Arm.


Running AI locally uses your computer’s own processing power, so how quickly it responds depends on your device. Local AI performance is still improving, and we’ll keep making it lighter and faster.


We can’t wait to see what you build!


Download[Opera One](https://www.opera.com/one) .
